slides.title: Feature Deep-Dive: Real-Time Collaboration Engine
slides.asset_payload:
Real-Time Collaboration Engine

Feature 01 of 03 · Owner: Platform Team · Target: July 31

What We're Building

  • Operational Transformation (OT) conflict resolution
  • Sub-100ms sync latency over WebSocket
  • Presence indicators & live cursor tracking
  • Offline-first with CRDT merge on reconnect

Success Metrics

  • P99 sync latency < 120ms
  • Zero data loss on concurrent edits
  • Support 50 simultaneous editors
  • 99.95% uptime SLA
Key Risk: CRDT library integration with our existing Postgres-backed data model requires a schema migration in week 3.
script_segments: Our headline feature for Q3 is the Real-Time Collaboration Engine — this has been the number one customer request for eighteen months.
At its core, we're implementing Operational Transformation to resolve edit conflicts when multiple users write to the same document simultaneously.
We're targeting a P99 sync latency below one hundred and twenty milliseconds, which puts us in the same bracket as Figma and Notion.
The biggest technical challenge is our CRDT integration — we need to run a Postgres schema migration in week three that will briefly lock a handful of tables.
We've already war-gamed that migration window with the SRE team, and we have a tested rollback procedure ready if anything goes sideways.
The Platform Team owns this end-to-end, with a hard ship date of July thirty-first — no slippage on this one.
slides.speaker_notes: If someone asks about backwards compatibility, confirm that read-only clients on the old protocol will continue to work through Q3 before the forced upgrade in Q4.

script_segments: Our final major initiative this quarter is the full revamp of our pricing and packaging model.
We're moving from a seat-based flat fee to a three-tier structure: a generous free Starter tier, a Pro tier at twenty-nine dollars per month, and a custom Enterprise tier.
The free tier is intentional — our data shows that teams who onboard for free convert to Pro at a thirty-four percent rate within ninety days.
Existing customers will be grandfathered on their current pricing until October first, giving them a full quarter to evaluate the new tiers.
The Beta invite goes out August first to our top two hundred power users, so we can catch any edge cases in the billing flow before the public launch on September fifteenth.
That wraps up the three major initiatives — let's open the floor for questions, and then I'll share the dependency matrix before we close.
slides.speaker_notes: Be ready for pushback on the grandfathering window — some enterprise customers have budget cycles that may not align. Escalate those cases to the VP of Sales directly.
